meta.hint: Check that a passport or creator ID is registered.

search.label: Paste an ID or link, or scan a QR code
search.hint: Passport IDs start with ODP-. Creator IDs look like C-123-456-789 (also B-, P-, or M-). You can paste text from a label, a link from this site, or tap the square button to scan a QR code.

result.badToken: That doesn’t look like a passport ID, creator ID, or a link from this site. Passport IDs start with ODP-. Creator IDs look like C-123-456-789.
result.loadFail: Can’t load registration data right now. Check your internet connection and try again.
result.notRegisteredBody: This ID does not exist in the registry. The object may not be registered, or the ID may be incorrect.
result.creatorNotFoundBody: This Creator ID does not exist in the registry, or the ID may be incorrect.

proof.lead: Separate tool from registry verify above: prove control of the creator wallet for a passport — no gas. The recovered signer must match passport.creator on-chain. This is key control, not legal authorship.
proof.panelSignHint: Connect the creator wallet, enter the passport Human ID, then sign. Copy the message + signature or the JSON bundle for the verifier.
proof.panelVerifyHint: Paste the exact message and signature from the creator. The page checks EIP-191 recovery against the passport’s on-chain creator (needs RPC + NET.contract).

doc.lead: If a creator recorded a file hash on a v0.2 contract (generation ≥ 2), drop the same file here. The page hashes it locally and checks the registry — no upload.

qr.title: Scan QR
qr.hint: Point the camera at the QR code on the label or screen.

time.onChainUtcHint: The chain stores a Unix timestamp in seconds; the registry treats it as a UTC instant.
time.localFromJsonHint: Wall-clock time and IANA zone as recorded when the passport file was built — the same instant as above.
